text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself — and you are the easiest person to fool.
author: Richard P. Feynman

text: Science is the belief in the ignorance of experts.
author: Richard P. Feynman

text: As far as the laws of mathematics refer to reality, they are not certain; and as far as they are certain, they do not refer to reality.
author: Albert Einstein

text: God does not play dice with the universe.
author: Albert Einstein

text: What we observe is not nature itself, but nature exposed to our method of questioning.
author: Werner Heisenberg

text: In so far as a scientific statement speaks about reality, it must be falsifiable.
author: Karl Popper

text: Our knowledge can only be finite, while our ignorance must necessarily be infinite.
author: Karl Popper

text: Normal science ... is puzzle-solving.
author: Thomas S. Kuhn

text: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.
author: Carl Sagan

text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
author: Isaac Newton

text: Science is built up of facts as a house is built of stones; but an accumulation of facts is no more a science than a heap of stones is a house.
author: Henri Poincaré

text: When you can measure what you are speaking about, and express it in numbers, you know something about it.
author: William Thomson (Lord Kelvin)

text: The theory of probabilities is at bottom nothing but common sense reduced to calculus.
author: Pierre-Simon Laplace

text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
author: Charles Darwin

text: Far better an approximate answer to the right question, which is often vague, than an exact answer to the wrong question, which can always be made precise.
author: John W. Tukey

text: All models are wrong, but some are useful.
author: George E. P. Box

text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
author: Alan M. Turing

text: Not only is the universe stranger than we imagine, it is stranger than we can imagine.
author: J. B. S. Haldane

text: We know more than we can tell.
author: Michael Polanyi

text: The unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences.
author: Eugene P. Wigner

text: A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence.
author: David Hume

text: Nature, to be commanded, must be obeyed.
author: Francis Bacon

text: A physical experiment is not simply the observation of a phenomenon; it is, besides, the theoretical interpretation of this phenomenon.
author: Pierre Duhem
source: The Aim and Structure of Physical Theory (1906)

text: The good thing about science is that it’s true whether or not you believe in it.
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson

text: Make everything as simple as possible, but not simpler.
author: Albert Einstein
